evals.prompt: /native-motion Settings의 @expo/ui ListItem이 밋밋해 보여. 누를 때마다 scale 0.97 애니메이션을 넣어서 더 살아있게 만들어줘.
evals.expected_output: The response identifies the ListItem as an @expo/ui native control, inspects the Host boundary, existing native feedback, and supported control or SwiftUI modifier surface, then rejects generic RN press scaling unless device evidence establishes a missing state signal.
expectations: It classifies the ListItem and its containing subtree as @expo/ui-owned rather than React Native-owned.
It inspects or cites the current Host boundary, native control behavior, and installed @expo/ui capability surface before proposing code.
It does not blindly apply the web-style scale 0.97 recipe.
It does not equate native ownership with an absence of configurable motion.
It preserves native feedback unless a concrete product or device observation justifies a supported owner-local change.

evals.prompt: /native-motion 채팅에서 맨 아래로 버튼이 갑자기 나타났다 사라져. 자연스럽게 바꿔줘.
evals.expected_output: The response identifies the button as an RN overlay, uses a focused Reanimated enter/exit treatment with system reduced-motion behavior, preserves virtualized scrolling, and verifies both appearance directions on the simulator.
expectations: It classifies the button as React Native-owned even though the app also uses @expo/ui elsewhere.
It keeps Expo Router navigation and the message list's virtualization out of the change.
It handles Reduce Motion and both entering and exiting behavior.
It adds focused test coverage where mechanically useful and requires device or recording verification for feel.

evals.prompt: /native-motion 채팅방을 열 때 화면 전환이 조금 느린 것 같아. Reanimated로 감싸서 더 빠르게 고쳐줘.
evals.expected_output: The response recognizes the route transition as native-stack-owned, inspects supported Expo Router animation, duration, presentation, and gesture configuration plus the running transition, and does not add a second Reanimated wrapper around it.
expectations: It classifies push and interactive back behavior as system-owned.
It investigates current Expo Router animation, duration, presentation, and gesture options plus runtime evidence before accepting the speed diagnosis.
It rejects layering an RN transition around the native stack.
It treats supported owner-level configuration as a real candidate rather than declaring the route untouchable.
If a real issue remains, it limits changes to supported owner-level configuration.

evals.prompt: /native-motion 앱이 좀 정적인 것 같아. 전체적으로 애니메이션 넣을 곳을 점검해줘.
evals.expected_output: The response performs a read-only renderer-aware opportunity audit, reports a small set of justified candidates, and includes rejected native, high-frequency, and content-stability cases.
expectations: It inventories system, @expo/ui, RN, and mixed boundaries plus each owner's configuration or modifier surface before proposing motion.
It keeps the audit read-only because the user asked to inspect rather than implement.
It reports purpose, frequency, owner, and reduced-motion behavior for surviving candidates.
It includes rejected candidates and does not turn the request into an animation wishlist.

evals.prompt: /native-motion RN 화면 위의 @expo/ui Host와 오류 overlay를 한 덩어리처럼 scale 전환해도 되는지 리뷰해줘.
evals.expected_output: The response splits ownership between the complete Host subtree and RN overlay, rejects an animation that reaches through the renderer boundary, and suggests owner-local continuity if motion is justified.
expectations: It identifies the mixed boundary instead of selecting one renderer for the whole screen.
It keeps the Host subtree self-contained.
It does not apply a Reanimated transform to SwiftUI leaves or duplicate Host wrappers around controls.
It returns review findings without modifying code.

evals.prompt: /native-motion Google 로그인 버튼 press 애니메이션을 리뷰해줘. Emil 스킬처럼 scale 0.97이 없으면 문제인지 봐줘.
evals.expected_output: The response recognizes the RN Pressable and vendor-owned visual constraints, verifies the existing pressed-opacity feedback, and does not flag absent scale as a defect by itself.
expectations: It classifies the outer interaction as RN-owned while preserving Google's brand-owned appearance.
It notices the existing pressed opacity feedback.
It treats scale as optional rather than a universal Pressable requirement.
It keeps the review read-only and cites concrete code and decision evidence.

evals.prompt: /native-motion 새 메시지를 보낼 때마다 haptic과 버블 등장 애니메이션을 추가해줘.
evals.expected_output: The response gates the high-frequency request, preserves chat readability and scroll behavior, and either rejects repeated haptics and decorative row entrances or narrows them to a justified causal state with reduced-motion behavior.
expectations: It accounts for message frequency and the fact that streaming content is already changing.
It does not add haptics to every message without a meaningful event distinction.
It preserves virtualized-list and user-away-from-bottom behavior.
Any surviving motion has a named purpose and a Reduce Motion alternative.

evals.prompt: /native-motion FormSubmitButton의 label 옆 ProgressView가 갑자기 나타나. @expo/ui니까 시스템 기본만 유지하고 끝내면 되는지 검토해줘.
evals.expected_output: The response identifies a self-contained @expo/ui Host subtree, inspects the installed SwiftUI animation, withAnimation, and related modifier capabilities, and decides whether the pending-state change needs owner-local continuity without using Reanimated through the boundary.
expectations: It classifies the Button, Row, Text, and ProgressView state change as @expo/ui-owned.
It inspects exact installed @expo/ui animation APIs before deciding what is possible.
It does not reject the opportunity merely because native controls already animate.
It keeps any surviving animation within the existing Host subtree and does not wrap SwiftUI leaves in Reanimated.
It names a Reduce Motion alternative and requires simulator verification for layout stability.
